question:
Match Column-A with Column-B

Column-A: i. G1 | ii. S | iii. G2 | iv. M

Column-B: a. Cell synthesises a complete copy of the DNA | b. First gap phase, the cell grows physically larger | c. Cell begins to reorganise its contents in preparation for mitosis | d. Cell divides its copied DNA and cytoplasm to make two new cells
solution_text:
The correct answer is i-b, ii-a, iii-c, iv-d.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The cell cycle has four phases — G1, S, G2 (together called Interphase) and M (Mitosis). (कोशिका चक्र — G1, S, G2, M प्रावस्थाएँ)

 

• G1 (Gap 1) phase — matches 'b': This is the first gap/growth phase, in which the cell grows physically larger, copies organelles and makes the molecular building blocks it will need in later steps.

 

• S (Synthesis) phase — matches 'a': The cell synthesises a complete copy of the DNA in its nucleus; the amount of DNA effectively doubles.

 

• G2 (Gap 2) phase — matches 'c': The cell grows more and reorganises its contents (produces microtubules etc.) in preparation for mitosis.

 

• M (Mitosis) phase — matches 'd': The cell divides its copied DNA and cytoplasm, producing two new (daughter) cells.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• G1, S and G2 together constitute Interphase, the longest part of the cell cycle, during which the cell is metabolically active but not yet dividing.

 

• Mitosis (M phase) itself is further divided into prophase, metaphase, anaphase and telophase, followed by cytokinesis.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 2 (i-c, ii-a, iii-b, iv-d): Incorrect because it swaps the descriptions of G1 and G2.

 

• Option 3 (i-a, ii-b, iii-c, iv-d): Incorrect because it swaps the descriptions of G1 and S.

 

• Option 4 (i-b, ii-a, iii-d, iv-c): Incorrect because it swaps the descriptions of G2 and M.

question: If Q = net charge, t = time, then which of the following equations is correct?
solution_text:
The correct answer is I = Q/t.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Electric current (I) is defined as the rate of flow of electric charge (Q) with respect to time (t). (विद्युत धारा — आवेश/समय)

 

• Mathematically, this relationship is expressed as I = Q/t, where Q is the net charge (in coulombs) that flows past a point in a conductor and t is the time (in seconds) taken.

 

• The SI unit of current is the ampere (A), defined as 1 coulomb of charge flowing per second (1 A = 1 C/s).

 

• Rearranging the formula gives Q = I × t, i.e., charge equals current multiplied by time — this is the form used to calculate total charge transferred.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Current is a scalar quantity, even though it has a direction of conventional flow (from positive to negative terminal, opposite to actual electron flow).

 

• Ohm's Law, V = IR, relates current to voltage (V) and resistance (R), and is a separate but related concept in the study of electricity.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 (t = Q × I): Incorrect; this equation is dimensionally and physically wrong — it does not represent any standard relationship between charge, current and time.

 

• Option 3 (Q = I/t): Incorrect; this inverts the correct relationship — it should be Q = I × t, not I/t.

 

• Option 4 (I = Q × t): Incorrect; multiplying charge by time does not give current — current is charge divided by time, not multiplied.

question: With which instrument do the sisters Lalita and Nandini identify?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Violin.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• M. Lalitha and M. Nandini, popularly known as the "Violin Sisters" or "Mysore Sisters", are a well-known Carnatic classical violin duo from India. (वायलिन बहनें — ललिता और नंदिनी)

 

• They are the daughters of the renowned violinist Mysore M. Nagaraj and grew up in a family deeply rooted in Carnatic classical music.

 

• The sisters perform violin duets together and are recognised for carrying forward the Mysore school of violin playing, known for its distinctive style within Carnatic music.

 

• They have performed extensively at major Carnatic music sabhas and festivals across India and abroad.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The violin was adapted into Carnatic music in the 18th-19th century and is now an integral accompanying (and solo) instrument in South Indian classical concerts.

 

• Other notable Carnatic violinists include Lalgudi G. Jayaraman, T. N. Krishnan, and the brother duo Ganesh-Kumaresh.

 

NOTE

 

• Mandolin (Option 1): Popularised in Carnatic music by artists such as U. Srinivas, not associated with Lalita and Nandini.

 

• Sarod (Option 3): A Hindustani classical string instrument, associated with artists like Amjad Ali Khan, unrelated to this duo.

 

• Flute (Option 4): A wind instrument; well-known Carnatic flautists include N. Ramani and T. R. Mahalingam, not Lalita and Nandini.

question: Guru Nileshwar Mukharjee is the exponent of which of the following Indian classical dance forms?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Manipuri.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Guru Nileshwar Mukharjee was a celebrated exponent and propagator of the Manipuri dance style. (मणिपुरी नृत्य — गुरु नीलेश्वर मुखर्जी)

 

• He gave a Ras Lila performance in Sylhet in 1920, which so impressed Rabindranath Tagore that Tagore invited him to Shantiniketan, a pivotal event that helped bring Manipuri dance to wider national and international recognition.

 

• Manipuri dance is one of the eight classical dance forms of India, originating in the state of Manipur, and is deeply associated with Vaishnavite themes, especially the Ras Lila depicting the life of Radha and Krishna.

 

• The dance style is characterised by graceful, fluid and delicate movements, minimal facial expression compared to other classical forms, and elaborate traditional costumes (Kumil/Potloi).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other important exponents of Manipuri dance include Guru Bipin Singh (founder of Manipuri Nartanalaya) and the Jhaveri sisters.

 

• Tagore was instrumental in introducing Manipuri dance into the curriculum at Visva-Bharati University, Shantiniketan.

 

NOTE

 

• Sattriya (Option 1): Classical dance of Assam, originating in Vaishnavite monasteries (sattras) founded by Srimanta Sankardeva.

 

• Odissi (Option 3): Classical dance of Odisha, closely linked to temple traditions (e.g., Jagannath Temple, Puri).

 

• Kathak (Option 4): Classical dance form of North India, known for its intricate footwork and spins, with gharanas at Jaipur, Lucknow and Banaras.

question: Which of the following festivals is organised by the Government of Karnataka, usually in January, to celebrate the grandeur of temples at a UNESCO heritage site?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pattadakal Dance Festival.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Pattadakal Dance Festival is organised annually, usually in January, by the Department of Kannada and Culture, Government of Karnataka. (पट्टदकल नृत्य महोत्सव — कर्नाटक)

 

• It is held at Pattadakal, a UNESCO World Heritage Site in Bagalkot district, Karnataka, famous for its cluster of 7th-8th century Chalukyan temples (a fusion of North Indian Nagara and South Indian Dravida styles).

 

• The festival celebrates the architectural grandeur of the Pattadakal temples (such as the Virupaksha and Mallikarjuna temples) as a backdrop for classical and folk dance performances by artists from across the country.

 

• Pattadakal was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1987.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Karnataka also hosts other heritage-linked cultural festivals such as the Hampi Utsav at the Hampi UNESCO site.

 

• The Virupaksha Temple at Pattadakal was built by Queen Lokamahadevi to commemorate her husband Vikramaditya II's victory over the Pallavas.

 

NOTE

 

• Kambala Festival (Option 1): A traditional buffalo race held in coastal Karnataka (Dakshina Kannada/Udupi), not a temple/heritage-site festival.

 

• Karaga Festival (Option 3): A Hindu festival celebrated mainly in Bengaluru, associated with the Draupadi/Dharmaraya Swamy Temple, not linked to a UNESCO site.

 

• Hoysala Festival (Option 4): Not a standard officially recognised Karnataka government cultural festival matching this description; the Hoysala temples (Belur, Halebidu) were inscribed as a UNESCO site only in 2023, after this exam.

question: In which Five-Year Plan, was the Mahalanobis Model started?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Second.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Mahalanobis Model, developed by the statistician Prof. P. C. Mahalanobis, was adopted for India's Second Five-Year Plan (1956-61). (महालनोबिस मॉडल — द्वितीय पंचवर्षीय योजना)

 

• The model emphasised rapid industrialisation, with a focus on developing heavy and basic industries (capital goods sector) as the key driver of long-term economic growth.

 

• It is also known as the "Nehru-Mahalanobis model", since it strongly shaped Jawaharlal Nehru's vision of a state-led, self-reliant industrial economy.

 

• Under this plan, institutions like several IITs and major public sector steel plants (e.g., Bhilai, Durgapur, Rourkela) were established.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The First Five-Year Plan (1951-56) was based on the Harrod-Domar model, focusing on agriculture.

 

• The Third Five-Year Plan (1961-66) continued to build on industrialisation but faced setbacks due to wars (1962, 1965) and droughts.

 

NOTE

 

• Fourth (Option 2): The Fourth Plan (1969-74) focused on the goals of "growth with stability" and "self-reliance", not the Mahalanobis Model.

 

• Third (Option 3): The Third Plan continued industrial goals but was not where the Mahalanobis Model was first introduced.

 

• First (Option 4): The First Plan was based on the Harrod-Domar model, prioritising agriculture and irrigation, not the Mahalanobis Model.

question: The Basketball centre line is part of the:
solution_text:
The correct answer is back court.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In basketball, the centre line (division line) runs parallel to the end lines and divides the court into two equal halves. (बास्केटबॉल केंद्र रेखा — बैक कोर्ट)

 

• As per official basketball rules, a team's backcourt consists of their own basket, the inbounds part of the backboard, and that part of the playing court limited by the end line behind their own basket, the two side lines, and the centre line — the centre line itself is considered part of the backcourt.

 

• This rule is significant for enforcing the 8-second backcourt violation, where the offensive team must advance the ball from the backcourt into the frontcourt within 8 seconds.

 

• The frontcourt is the half of the court containing the opposing team's basket, where the offensive team attacks.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• A basketball court is 28 m long and 15 m wide as per FIBA standards.

 

• The restricted area (the painted key/lane) is near each basket and is used to determine charging/blocking fouls.

 

NOTE

 

• front court (Option 1): Incorrect; the centre line belongs to the backcourt, not the frontcourt, as per official rules.

 

• restricted area (Option 3): This refers to the semicircular zone under the basket, unrelated to the centre line.

 

• middle court (Option 4): Not an official basketball court zone/term.

question: From the point of view of commerce, the busiest ocean of the world is ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Atlantic ocean.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Atlantic Ocean is regarded as the busiest ocean in the world from a commercial/trade standpoint. (अटलांटिक महासागर — सर्वाधिक व्यस्त वाणिज्यिक महासागर)

 

• It connects the major industrialised and trading regions of Europe, North America, South America and Africa, carrying some of the world's heaviest volumes of shipping traffic.

 

• It is the second-largest ocean in the world (after the Pacific) and hosts crucial trade routes such as the North Atlantic shipping lanes.

 

• Major ports on the Atlantic (e.g., New York, Rotterdam, London) handle enormous volumes of international trade, making it central to global commerce.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Pacific Ocean is the largest ocean by area in the world.

 

• The Indian Ocean is the third-largest ocean, important for trade between Asia, Africa and the Middle East, especially oil shipping routes.

 

NOTE

 

• Pacific ocean (Option 1): Largest by area, but not considered the busiest for commerce compared to the Atlantic.

 

• Indian ocean (Option 2): Important for trade, particularly oil, but ranks below the Atlantic in overall commercial traffic.

 

• Arctic ocean (Option 3): Smallest and shallowest ocean, largely ice-covered, with minimal commercial shipping traffic.

question: On which river, the first night navigation mobile application in rivers in India was launched for ferries?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Brahmaputra.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Government of Assam, in collaboration with IIT Madras, launched India's first night navigation mobile application for ferries operating on the Brahmaputra river in 2022. (रात्रि नौवहन ऐप — ब्रह्मपुत्र नदी)

 

• The app uses GPS and mapping technology to guide ferry pilots safely across the river during night hours, when visibility and shifting sandbars make navigation risky.

 

• This made Assam the first state in India to introduce a dedicated night navigation system for river ferry services.

 

• The initiative aims to improve safety of passengers and cargo ferried across the Brahmaputra, especially for connectivity to remote riverine (char) areas.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Brahmaputra is one of the major rivers of Asia, originating in Tibet and flowing through Arunachal Pradesh and Assam before entering Bangladesh.

 

• The Namami Brahmaputra Festival is also organised by the Assam government to promote the river's cultural and economic significance.

 

NOTE

 

• Ganga (Option 2): India's longest river with significant inland waterway projects (e.g., Jal Marg Vikas Project), but not where this specific app was first launched.

 

• Kaveri (Option 3): A major river of South India, not associated with this initiative.

 

• Son (Option 4): A tributary of the Ganga in central India, not associated with this initiative.

question: Minhaj-i-Siraj was a chronicler during the rule of ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sultan Iltutmish.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Minhaj-i-Siraj (Minhaj-us-Siraj) was a Persian historian and chronicler of the Delhi Sultanate, best known for authoring "Tabaqat-i-Nasiri". (मिन्हाज-उस-सिराज — इल्तुतमिश काल का इतिहासकार)

 

• He arrived in Delhi in 1228 CE, during the reign of Sultan Shamsuddin Iltutmish, and began his career as a chronicler and religious scholar at the Delhi court under Iltutmish's patronage.

 

• He later rose to prominence and served as Qazi (chief judge) of Delhi, continuing his historical writing into the reign of Sultan Nasiruddin Mahmud.

 

• His work Tabaqat-i-Nasiri is one of the most important primary sources for the early history of the Delhi Sultanate, covering events from the rise of Islam up to 1260 CE.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Iltutmish (r. 1211-1236) is considered the real founder of the Delhi Sultanate, consolidating the Sultanate and introducing the Iqta system and silver tanka/copper jital coinage.

 

• Iltutmish was also responsible for completing the construction of the Qutub Minar.

 

NOTE

 

• Qutbuddin Aybak (Option 2): Founder of the Mamluk (Slave) Dynasty; Minhaj's career at the Delhi court began after Aybak's reign.

 

• Ghiyasuddin Balban (Option 3): A later Sultan (r. 1266-1287) of the Mamluk dynasty; Minhaj's chronicling work began earlier, under Iltutmish.

 

• Alauddin Khalji (Option 4): Founder ruler of the Khalji dynasty (r. 1296-1316), much later than Minhaj-i-Siraj's period of activity.

question: Joint Liability Group is usually an informal group that consists of _________ individuals who seek loans against mutual guarantee.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 4-10.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A Joint Liability Group (JLG) is an informal group of 4 to 10 individuals who come together to avail bank loans, either individually or through the group mechanism, against mutual guarantee. (संयुक्त देयता समूह — 4 से 10 सदस्य)

 

• JLGs are primarily meant for small/marginal farmers, tenant farmers, and rural micro-entrepreneurs who lack proper title/documents for land or formal collateral needed for conventional bank loans.

 

• Since members of a JLG mutually guarantee the loan repayment of each other, this reduces the risk for banks and improves credit access for the group members.

 

• The JLG model was promoted by NABARD (National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development) to widen the flow of institutional credit to underserved rural populations.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• JLGs differ from Self-Help Groups (SHGs), which typically have 10-20 members and focus more broadly on savings and credit.

 

• NABARD has piloted and refined the JLG model since the mid-2000s to promote financial inclusion in rural India.

 

NOTE

 

• 1-3 (Option 1): Too small a group size to constitute a standard JLG as defined by NABARD.

 

• 15-20 (Option 2): This range is closer to the typical size of a Self-Help Group (SHG), not a JLG.

 

• 20-30 (Option 4): Too large; this does not match the standard NABARD-defined JLG size.

question: Which of the following can alter the boundary of a state or change its name?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Parliament.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Under Article 3 of the Constitution of India, the Parliament of India has the power to form new states, alter the boundaries, area or name of an existing state. (अनुच्छेद 3 — संसद, राज्यों की सीमा/नाम परिवर्तन)

 

• Parliament can do this by a simple majority (ordinary law), though the President must first refer the relevant Bill to the Legislature of the affected state to get its views, within a specified time period.

 

• Importantly, the views of the state legislature are only recommendatory and not binding on Parliament — Parliament can still proceed even if the state disagrees.

 

• This provision reflects that Indian states do not have territorial integrity guaranteed against the Union, distinguishing India's federal structure from that of countries like the USA.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Article 4 provides that laws made under Article 3 (for state reorganisation) are not to be considered as amendments to the Constitution under Article 368.

 

• Examples of states formed/altered under Article 3 include the creation of Telangana (2014) and the reorganisation of Jammu & Kashmir (2019).

 

NOTE

 

• State government (Option 1): State governments can only recommend/give their views; they cannot unilaterally alter their own boundaries or name.

 

• Supreme Court (Option 3): The judiciary interprets the Constitution and adjudicates disputes but has no power to alter state boundaries or names.

 

• High Court (Option 4): Like the Supreme Court, High Courts have no constitutional authority to alter state boundaries or names.

question: Ganga Sagar Mela is conducted at the mouth of the river Hooghly in ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is West Bengal.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Ganga Sagar Mela is a major annual Hindu pilgrimage fair held at Sagar Island (Gangasagar), where the Hooghly river (a distributary of the Ganga) meets the Bay of Bengal, in West Bengal. (गंगासागर मेला — पश्चिम बंगाल)

 

• It is held every year on Makar Sankranti (mid-January), when pilgrims take a holy dip at the confluence, believed to cleanse sins.

 

• The site is associated with the legend of King Bhagiratha, who is said to have brought the Ganga down to earth to liberate the souls of his ancestors, and with the Kapil Muni Temple, located at Sagar Island.

 

• It is often referred to as "Mini Kumbh Mela" due to the massive number of devotees it attracts, making it one of the largest religious congregations in India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Sagar Island lies in the Sundarbans delta region of West Bengal, at the confluence of the Hooghly river and the Bay of Bengal.

 

• The mela involves significant logistical arrangements by the West Bengal government, given the large influx of pilgrims from across India.

 

NOTE

 

• Bihar (Option 2): Known for other religious sites/fairs like Sonepur Mela, not the Ganga Sagar Mela.

 

• Goa (Option 3): Not located on the Ganga/Hooghly river system; known for different festivals.

 

• Andhra Pradesh (Option 4): Not associated with the Hooghly river or Ganga Sagar Mela.

question: ______ is a change of position.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Motion.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Motion is defined in physics as a change in the position of an object with respect to time and its surroundings (a reference point). (गति — स्थिति में परिवर्तन)

 

• An object is said to be in motion if its position changes continuously with respect to a fixed reference point/observer over a period of time.

 

• Speed and velocity are quantities that describe how fast the position changes (rate of change of distance/displacement), not the change of position itself.

 

• Distance is the total path length covered by an object during motion, which is a consequence/measure of motion, but not its definition.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Motion can be classified into types such as translatory, rotatory, oscillatory and vibratory motion based on the nature of movement.

 

• The study of motion without considering the causes (forces) behind it is called kinematics, a branch of classical mechanics.

 

NOTE

 

• Speed (Option 1): Defined as the rate of change of distance with time (a scalar quantity); it describes how fast motion occurs, not the change of position itself.

 

• Velocity (Option 2): Defined as the rate of change of displacement with time (a vector quantity); again describes the rate, not the change of position.

 

• Distance (Option 4): The total length of the path travelled; it is a measurable outcome of motion, not the definition of a change of position.

question: FIFA U-19 Women's World Cup 2022 will be organised by ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is India.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• India hosted the FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup 2022 (referred to in this question by the source paper), held from 11 to 30 October 2022. (फीफा अंडर-17 महिला विश्व कप — भारत)

 

• Matches were played across four venues: Bhubaneswar, Goa, Navi Mumbai, and Odisha's Kalinga Stadium.

 

• This tournament was notable as India's first-ever FIFA World Cup hosting of any kind (men's or women's, any age group).

 

• The tournament was won by Spain, who defeated Colombia in the final.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• India had earlier hosted the FIFA U-17 Men's World Cup in 2017, won by England.

 

• The All India Football Federation (AIFF) was the host organisation working with FIFA for the 2022 tournament.

 

NOTE

 

• England (Option 1): Hosted other FIFA tournaments in the past (e.g., 2019 Women's World Cup was in France; England hosted UEFA Women's Euro 2022), but not this event.

 

• Brazil (Option 2): Has hosted major football tournaments like the 2014 FIFA World Cup, not this one.

 

• the US (Option 3): Frequently hosts FIFA youth tournaments, but not the 2022 edition, which was hosted by India.

question: “All India Muslim League” was formed at Dacca in ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1906.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The All India Muslim League was founded on 30 December 1906 at Dacca (present-day Dhaka), during the annual session of the All India Muhammadan Educational Conference. (मुस्लिम लीग — 1906, ढाका)

 

• It was formed under the leadership of Nawab Salimullah Khan of Dacca, along with other prominent Muslim leaders, following a deputation to Viceroy Lord Minto earlier in 1906 (the Simla Deputation).

 

• The League's founding objectives included promoting loyalty to the British Government, safeguarding the political rights of Muslims, and preventing the rise of hostility towards other communities.

 

• The League later played a central role in Indian politics, including the demand for separate electorates, granted under the Indian Councils Act, 1909 (Morley-Minto Reforms).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Indian National Congress, in contrast, was founded earlier in 1885 by A.O. Hume.

 

• The Muslim League later demanded a separate nation, leading to the Lahore Resolution of 1940 and eventually the creation of Pakistan in 1947.

 

NOTE

 

• 1900 (Option 1):, 1904 (Option 2) and 1902 (Option 3): These years do not correspond to the actual founding date of the All India Muslim League, which was 1906.

question: Chittaranjan Das was the political guru of which of the following personalities?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Subhash Chandra Bose.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Chittaranjan (C.R.) Das, popularly known as "Deshbandhu", was the political mentor (guru) of Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose. (देशबंधु चितरंजन दास — सुभाष चंद्र बोस के राजनीतिक गुरु)

 

• C.R. Das brought young Subhash Chandra Bose into active politics in Bengal and deeply influenced his nationalist ideology.

 

• Together with Motilal Nehru, C.R. Das founded the Swaraj Party in 1923, advocating entry into legislative councils to obstruct British governance from within.

 

• C.R. Das served as the Mayor of Calcutta in 1924, appointing Subhash Chandra Bose as the Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of the Calcutta Municipal Corporation.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• C.R. Das passed away in 1925, and Subhash Chandra Bose continued to honour his legacy throughout his political career.

 

• The Swaraj Party, co-founded by C.R. Das, was formed after differences arose within the Congress over the Non-Cooperation Movement's suspension (1922).

 

NOTE

 

• Mahatama Gandhi (Option 2): Gandhi's own political mentor was Gopal Krishna Gokhale, not C.R. Das.

 

• Jawaharlal Nehru (Option 3): Nehru's political mentor was primarily his own father, Motilal Nehru, and later Gandhi.

 

• Bhagat Singh (Option 4): Bhagat Singh was influenced by revolutionaries and ideologues like Lala Lajpat Rai, not C.R. Das.

question: Which of the following pairs of ‘Dynasty – Ruled region’ is correctly matched? I. Shakas – North west and north India II. Vakatakas – Central and western India
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both I and II.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Both pairs are correctly matched. (शक और वाकाटक वंश — शासन क्षेत्र)

 

• Statement I is correct — Shakas (Scythians): The Shakas invaded India from Central Asia and established their rule primarily over north-western and northern India, including regions such as Punjab, Sindh, and parts of western India (e.g., the Western Kshatrapas in Gujarat/Malwa).

 

• Statement II is correct — Vakatakas: The Vakataka dynasty ruled over central and western India (present-day Maharashtra, Vidarbha, and parts of Madhya Pradesh) from around the 3rd to 5th century CE, and were notable contemporaries and matrimonial allies of the Gupta Empire.

 

• The Vakatakas are also remembered for their patronage of art and architecture, including contributions to the later phases of the Ajanta Caves.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The most famous Shaka ruler was Rudradaman I, known for the Junagadh Rock Inscription (a Sanskrit inscription about repairing the Sudarshana lake).

 

• The Vakataka ruler Prabhavatigupta (a Gupta princess) served as regent, illustrating close Gupta-Vakataka ties.

 

NOTE

 

• Neither I nor II (Option 1): Incorrect, as both statements are factually correct.

 

• Only I (Option 2): Incorrect, as it wrongly excludes Statement II, which is also correct.

 

• Only II (Option 3): Incorrect, as it wrongly excludes Statement I, which is also correct.

question: Who was appointed as India's chief G20 coordinator in April 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Harsh V Shringla.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Harsh Vardhan Shringla, a former Foreign Secretary of India, was appointed as India's Chief Coordinator for the G20 Presidency in April 2022. (जी20 समन्वयक — हर्षवर्धन श्रृंगला)

 

• He was tasked with overseeing the logistics, planning, and coordination for India's G20 Presidency, which India held from 1 December 2022 to 30 November 2023.

 

• Prior to this role, Shringla served as India's Ambassador to the United States and also as High Commissioner to Bangladesh.

 

• The G20 Summit 2023 was hosted in New Delhi, under the theme "Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam" (One Earth, One Family, One Future).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's G20 Sherpa for the presidency was Amitabh Kant (former NITI Aayog CEO).

 

• The G20 (Group of Twenty) is the premier forum for international economic cooperation, comprising 19 countries plus the European Union (and later the African Union).

 

NOTE

 

• Jasleen Kohli (Option 1):, C Muhammed Faizi (Option 3) and Abhishek Singh (Option 4): These are not the officials appointed as India's Chief G20 Coordinator; that role went to Harsh V Shringla.

question: The Purple revolution was launched by the Union Ministry of Science & Technology in Jammu and Kashmir. This revolution is related to cultivation of which crop?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lavender.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The "Purple Revolution" refers to the large-scale promotion of lavender cultivation in the Jammu and Kashmir region, under the Aroma Mission of CSIR (Council of Scientific and Industrial Research), which falls under the Union Ministry of Science & Technology. (पर्पल क्रांति — लैवेंडर की खेती)

 

• The initiative was pioneered largely in Doda district (Bhaderwah) of Jammu & Kashmir, helping farmers shift from traditional low-income crops to high-value lavender cultivation.

 

• The purple-coloured lavender flowers give the movement its name "Purple Revolution", and the produce is used for essential oils, perfumes, and cosmetics, boosting farmers' incomes.

 

• CSIR's Indian Institute of Integrative Medicine (IIIM), Jammu, played a key role in providing planting material and technical support to farmers under this mission.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Aroma Mission aims to bring together various stakeholders to promote the cultivation of aromatic crops for essential oils to boost the aroma industry.

 

• Other 'colour revolutions' in India include the Green Revolution (foodgrains), White Revolution (milk, Operation Flood) and Blue Revolution (fisheries).

 

NOTE

 

• Marigold (Option 1): Not linked to the Purple Revolution; grown widely across India mainly for flowers/garlands.

 

• Kashmiri Rose (Option 2): Also cultivated in J&K for essential oils but is not the crop behind the "Purple Revolution" branding.

 

• Himalayan Indigo (Option 4): Not associated with this government revolution/initiative.

question: The atomic number of lead is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is 82.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Lead (Pb) has an atomic number of 82, meaning it has 82 protons in its nucleus. (सीसा (लेड) — परमाणु क्रमांक 82)

 

• Lead's chemical symbol "Pb" is derived from its Latin name "Plumbum".

 

• Lead is a post-transition metal, known for being soft, dense, and having a relatively low melting point compared to other metals; it is widely used in batteries, radiation shielding, and alloys.

 

• It belongs to Group 14 (carbon group) and Period 6 of the modern periodic table.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Lead is the heaviest naturally occurring element that has a stable isotope and no observed radioactive decay under normal conditions (though very slow decay theoretically occurs for some isotopes).

 

• Excessive exposure to lead is toxic and can cause lead poisoning, which is why lead-based paints and leaded petrol have been phased out globally.

 

NOTE

 

• 81 (Option 1): This is the atomic number of Thallium (Tl), not lead.

 

• 78 (Option 2): This is the atomic number of Platinum (Pt), not lead.

 

• 79 (Option 4): This is the atomic number of Gold (Au), not lead.

question: Which of the following Articles of the Constitution of India deals with amendment in the Constitution?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 368.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 368 of the Indian Constitution, found in Part XX, deals with the "Power of Parliament to amend the Constitution and procedure therefor". (अनुच्छेद 368 — संविधान संशोधन)

 

• It empowers Parliament to amend any provision of the Constitution by way of addition, variation, or repeal, following the procedure laid down.

 

• The Constitution provides for three types of amendment procedures: by simple majority, by special majority, and by special majority with ratification by half the states.

 

• The Kesavananda Bharati case (1973) established that Parliament's amending power under Article 368 cannot alter the "Basic Structure" of the Constitution.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The first amendment to the Indian Constitution was made in 1951, adding provisions related to land reforms and freedom of speech restrictions, among others.

 

• Article 368 itself was substantially amended by the 24th Amendment Act, 1971, to affirm Parliament's constituent power explicitly.

 

NOTE

 

• Article 365 (Option 1): Deals with the effect of failure to comply with, or to give effect to, directions given by the Union to a state.

 

• Article 360 (Option 2): Deals with the proclamation of Financial Emergency.

 

• Article 355 (Option 4): Deals with the duty of the Union to protect states against external aggression and internal disturbance.

question: By which name is the historical road built by Sher Shah Suri known?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Grand trunk road.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Grand Trunk (GT) Road is one of Asia's oldest and longest major roads, significantly developed and extended by Sher Shah Suri during his reign (1540-1545 CE). (ग्रांड ट्रंक रोड — शेरशाह सूरी)

 

• Sher Shah Suri rebuilt and extended this road, originally tracing older trade routes, to connect Sonargaon (Bengal) to Peshawar (in present-day Pakistan), covering roughly 2,500 km.

 

• He is credited with setting up sarais (rest houses) at regular intervals along the road for travellers, along with wells and shade trees, greatly improving trade and communication across the empire.

 

• The road was later extended further by the British during colonial rule, eventually connecting Kabul to Kolkata (Chittagong in some descriptions).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Sher Shah Suri, founder of the Sur Empire, also introduced significant administrative and monetary reforms, including the Rupiya (silver coin), a precursor to the modern rupee.

 

• The GT Road today passes through India, Pakistan, and Bangladesh, and remains a vital transportation corridor.

 

NOTE

 

• Express way (Option 2):, Highway (Option 3) and Cart road (Option 4): These are generic modern terms and not the historical name by which Sher Shah Suri's road is specifically known.

question: The poverty ratio has declined to ______ in 2011-12 in rural India.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 30.9 percent.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per the Rangarajan Committee Report on Poverty, the rural poverty ratio in India declined to 30.9% in 2011-12, down from 39.6% in 2009-10. (ग्रामीण गरीबी अनुपात — 30.9% (2011-12), रंगराजन समिति)

 

• The C. Rangarajan Committee was constituted by the Planning Commission to review the methodology for measuring poverty, as an alternative to the earlier Tendulkar Committee methodology.

 

• The Rangarajan panel revised the poverty line upward compared to the Tendulkar Committee, resulting in a higher estimated poverty ratio for the same period.

 

• As per this report, the all-India poverty ratio for 2011-12 was 29.5%, with rural poverty at 30.9% and urban poverty at 26.4%.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Tendulkar Committee, using a different methodology, had estimated a lower rural poverty ratio of about 25.7% for the same year (2011-12) — a figure sometimes cited in other sources.

 

• The Rangarajan Committee report was submitted in 2014, recommending separate rural and urban poverty lines based on updated consumption baskets.

 

NOTE

 

• 20.9 percent (Option 1): Not the figure reported by the Rangarajan Committee for rural India in 2011-12.

 

• 25.9 percent (Option 3): Close to, but not the exact figure used in this question's answer key (which follows the Rangarajan estimate of 30.9%, not the Tendulkar-based ~25.7%).

 

• 35.9 percent (Option 4): Not the figure reported by the Rangarajan Committee for rural India in 2011-12.

question: In a lake ecosystem, the primary consumers are ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is zooplankton.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In a lake (pond) ecosystem, the food chain typically follows: phytoplankton (producers) → zooplankton (primary consumers) → small fish (secondary consumers) → large fish (tertiary consumers). (झील पारिस्थितिकी तंत्र — प्राथमिक उपभोक्ता: जूप्लैंकटन)

 

• Zooplankton are microscopic/small floating animals (e.g., water fleas, rotifers, small crustaceans) that feed directly on phytoplankton, making them the primary consumers (herbivores) of the aquatic food chain.

 

• Phytoplankton, being photosynthetic microscopic algae/plant-like organisms, occupy the position of primary producers, converting sunlight into chemical energy.

 

• This energy flow forms the base of the entire aquatic food web, ultimately supporting fish and other higher trophic-level organisms in the lake.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Trophic levels in any ecosystem generally follow the order: producers → primary consumers → secondary consumers → tertiary consumers → decomposers.

 

• Decomposers (bacteria and fungi) break down dead organic matter, recycling nutrients back into the ecosystem, but are not classified as "primary consumers".

 

NOTE

 

• phytoplankton (Option 2): These are the primary producers of a lake ecosystem, not primary consumers — they are eaten by zooplankton.

 

• bacteria (Option 3): Bacteria mainly function as decomposers, breaking down organic matter, not as primary consumers.

 

• fishes (Option 4): Small fish that eat zooplankton are typically classified as secondary consumers, not primary consumers.
